citeAs: Bisk, Y., Zellers, R., Le Bras, R., Gao, J., & Choi, Y. (2020). PIQA: Reasoning about Physical Commonsense in Natural Language. AAAI.
creator: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi (Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Microsoft Research AI, Carnegie Mellon University, University of Washington)
description: A benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning, consisting of multiple-choice questions about everyday situations with a preference for atypical solutions.
name: PIQA
publisher: Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Microsoft Research AI, Carnegie Mellon University, University of Washington
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed from the data.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (implied by references to HITs and turkerview.com)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were asked to glance at the instructions of an instructable and pull out or have it inspire them to construct two component tasks. They would then articulate the goal and how to achieve it, and provide a permutation to their own solution which makes it invalid.
rai:dataBiases: The authors note that reporting bias swamped the dataset when using unconstrained prompts, as people are drawn to prototypical solutions. To address this and flatten the distribution of referenced objects, they prompted annotations with links to instructables.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected by prompting annotators with links to instructables.com to inspire them to construct goal-solution pairs, including a valid solution and an incorrect trick solution.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The instructables website, a crowdsourced collection of instructions for doing everything from cooking to car repair.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset is cleaned of basic artifacts using the AFLite algorithm, which discards instances whose given feature representations are collectively highly indicative of the target label.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating language representations on their knowledge of physical commonsense.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: AFLite algorithm, which uses an ensemble of linear classifiers trained on random subsets of the data to determine whether pre-computed embeddings are strong indicators of the correct answer option.
